Her automatic thought is: Everyone will notice every mistake and conclude that I am incompetent. She rates the belief at 80 percent and her anxiety at 7 out of 10.
Coaching response The coach asks Maya to separate observable facts from predictions. Evidence supporting the thought is that she paused twice in her last presentation. Evidence against it is that colleagues asked useful follow-up questions, her manager approved the proposal, and no one criticized her competence.

A balanced alternative thought is: I may pause or make a small mistake, but I can still explain the main idea clearly. A pause does not prove incompetence. Maya then rates her belief in the original thought at 45 percent and her anxiety at 4 out of 10.

Behavioral Experiment Plan Before the next presentation, Maya will practice the opening for five minutes, deliberately allow one short pause, and record whether listeners remain engaged. She predicts that at least half the audience will react negatively. The observable measure is the number of negative comments or visible signs of disengagement.
